research.facts:
PCA Joins the 40-40 Club
**Confirmed Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- PCA (Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs CF, age 24) stole second base in the 1st inning on Sept. 24 vs. Miami Marlins at Wrigley Field
- The steal came on a leadoff walk off Tyler Phillips; PCA took off for 2nd on the first pitch thrown to Seiya Suzuki
- PCA's season total: 45 HR / 40 SB — making him the 7th member of the 40-40 club
- The 40-40 Club — all 7 members: Jose Canseco (Oakland A's, 1988), Barry Bonds (San Francisco Giants, 1996), Alex Rodriguez (Seattle Mariners, 1998), Alfonso Soriano (Washington Nationals, 2006), Ronald Acuña Jr. (Atlanta Braves, 2023), Shohei Ohtani (Los Angeles Dodgers, 2024), Pete Crow-Armstrong (Chicago Cubs, 2026)
- Wrigley crowd erupted with "MVP" chants; videoboard proclaimed the feat mid-game
- Cubs won 2-1. Matthew Boyd (10-5) went 7 innings, 1 ER; Ryan Zeferjahn closed with a perfect 9th (save No. 7)
- Seiya Suzuki also homered for Chicago
- With the win, Cubs (88-71) clinched an NL Wild Card berth — their second consecutive playoff appearance
- PCA is the third player in the last four seasons to join 40-40 (after Acuña 2023 and Ohtani 2024)
**Sources:** Washington Post; TSN; NBC DFW; Yahoo Sports; Chicago Sun-Times; dawindycity.com

research.facts:
Chicago's Double Clinch — Cubs and White Sox
**Confirmed Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- White Sox clinched a playoff berth Sept. 24 with a 9-1 rout of the Kansas City Royals
- Cubs clinched the same night with the 2-1 win over the Marlins — both teams clinched within minutes of each other
- The White Sox are the first team in MLB history to follow consecutive 100-loss seasons by reaching the playoffs
- Context: The 2024 Chicago White Sox lost 121 games — the most losses in MLB history in a single season
- GM Chris Getz; manager Will Venable; seven of nine starters have under two years of MLB experience
- The White Sox can still win the AL Central (trail the Guardians by 1 game with 3 games remaining)
- The Cubs are the 2026 NL Wild Card team (WC2); Wild Card Series begins September 29
**Sources:** FOX Sports; Bleacher Report; CBS Sports; MLB.com; ABC7 Chicago; Yahoo Sports; Axios Chicago

research.facts:
Aaron Judge Wild Card Status
**Confirmed Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Judge has a "moderate grade" right calf strain (soleus muscle)
- Injury occurred just 7 games after he returned from a right rib fracture — back on the 10-day IL immediately
- Has not resumed hitting as of September 24
- Manager Aaron Boone: team is "planning on him not being a part of" the Wild Card Series vs. Red Sox (begins Sept. 29)
- Boone has not officially ruled Judge out entirely
- Judge's own quote: "I'd like to be back by the postseason. That's definitely the plan."
- If the Wild Card round ends Thursday Oct. 1 (it's a best-of-3 series), Judge's window would be the ALDS
- Yankees are No. 4 AL seed vs. Boston Red Sox (WC series starts Sept. 29)
- Separate Yankees note: Clarke Schmidt placed on 15-day IL with right bicep neuritis — blow to postseason rotation depth
**Sources:** Bleacher Report; Yahoo Sports; FOX Sports; CBS Sports (three questions piece)
